messages:
marisol: quick q — I'm poking at a different canary model: 'harmonic' staged allocator instead of fixed percentage splits. idea: allocate traffic in small rhythmic bursts (1s windows) with token-aware pacing so we don't thrash KV caches. thoughts?

devin: interesting. why harmonic vs say exponential ramp?

marisol: two reasons: 1) smoother transient load on GPU memory (less long spike), 2) gives observer time to assess per-window regressions without waiting for large sample sizes. also easier to interleave probes across variants.

ankur: tradeoff is complexity in router state. bursts imply short-lived affinity decisions. do we want per-session sticky or per-request routing?

marisol: leaning per-session for chat flows where KV cache warmup matters. but need a fallback that can route request-level when session affinity fails.

samir: plausible fallback stack: 1) attempt session-affine route, 2) if unavailable, route to compatible variant (quantized or smaller context) with same API contract, 3) last resort global fallback model. keep fallback deterministic to avoid oscillation.

devin: deterministic fallback + backoff. also add a fast health probe that validates correctness metric (BLEU/lexical delta) on a small prompt set per-window. if drift > threshold, trigger immediate cutback.

ankur: how do we compute 'compatible variant'? metadata tag on model: "compatible-with:[parent, kv-schema-version, context-len]". runtime picks the closest match. example: model-a:q8 is compatible-with model-a:fp16.

sylvie: code sketch for router decision (pseudo):
```
if session_affine_available(session_id):
  route(session_id.variant)
else:
  candidate = pick_closest_compatible(primary_variant, fallback_budget)
  route(candidate)
```
we should also record why fallback happened for postmortem (quota, OOM, probe-failure).

marisol: agree on observability. add these fields to token logs: routed_variant, fallback_reason, probe_score. we'll surface in console as per-route slices.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-controller/feature/harmonic-allocator @marisol @devin (build #389) :rocket:

devin: ops note — ensure canary-controller can be toggled to literal percentage mode for accounts with strict billing predictability. some customers won't like burstiness.

marisol: yep, config will expose rollout_mode: [harmonic, steady_percent, manual]. default harmonic but override per-tenant.

ankur: question about KV invalidation: when we fallback to an incompatible quantization, we must drop session KV cache or we risk corruption. propose each variant gets a kv-namespace tag. router decides to clear or remap.

samir: clearing on fallback could spike latency. alternative: maintain per-variant cache with warmup hints. warmup hints: router can request prewarm on small async replica before flipping traffic.

sylvie: prewarm flow example: router tells serving pool: prewarm(model-a:q8, session_id) -> returns warm_token. only flip when warm_token present or after x ms fallback. reduces error budget consumption.

marisol: solid. we'll need cross-team agreement on memory budget for per-variant prewarm pools. open question: who pays for prewarm? dedicated vs hosted customers differ.

devin: for hosted default, allow limited prewarm budget and evict LRU. for dedicated contracts expose param in Dedicated config.

samir: telemetry acceptance criteria: detect 3 things in first 5m windows - latency percentile regression, token-accuracy delta (eval set), error rate. if 2/3 breach, auto-scale fallback to safe variant. keep human-in-loop notification channel.

marisol: last: API contract boundary — function/tool calls need deterministic fallback too. if tool contract changes across variants we must reject swap and fallback earlier. add 'contract-check' to canary-controller.

ankur: agreement: router + canary-controller will expose a simple JSON API for contract-check:
```
POST /v1/canary/check
{ "primary": "model-a:2026-03-01", "candidate": "model-a:q8" }
```
returns ok|incompatible + reason.

devin: next steps: I'll open a tiny RFC PR outlining: harmonic allocator semantics, fallback state machine, prewarm protocol, and observability fields. include a flow diagram for session vs request routing.

marisol: awesome. ping me on the RFC. thanks all. :thumbsup:
